subject: Vision & Philosophy: Computational Rigor Meets Creative Expression
paragraphs: I am a Computational Physicist (Double Degree in Physics & Mathematics, MSc in Plasma Physics) and HPC Scientific Software Engineer at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC). My career has bridged mathematical formalism with real-world, high-stakes computational problems across supercomputing, energy, and aerospace engineering.
Across diverse roles and European institutions, I have developed a unified methodology for tackling complex physical systems:

methods.name: Non-Convex Multi-Dimensional Optimization
methods.summary: Navigating non-convex, multimodal parameter spaces using heuristic search and simulated annealing. Designed non-planar radar antenna geometry in MATLAB to optimize radiation patterns and beam directivity under tight geometric constraints.

methods.name: Industrial Data Science & Sensor Anomaly Detection
methods.summary: Building end-to-end Python pipelines to analyze high-frequency SCADA time-series telemetry from offshore wind farms. Engineered predictive classification models with Scikit-Learn and Pandas to anticipate mechanical degradation and optimize turbine maintenance.

methods.name: Particle Tracking & Symplectic Integration
methods.summary: Developing high-order symplectic particle integrators to trace charged particle trajectories and loss cones through turbulent magnetic fields. Translating kinetic and magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) equations into scalable parallel diagnostics.

closing_paragraphs: Treating agentic workflows and LLMs as fluid thinking partners enables seamless transitions between C++/Fortran HPC kernels, microcontroller firmware, and interactive web tools.

Whether profiling parallel efficiency on Tier-0 supercomputers (MN5, LUMI), modeling complex physical dynamics, or designing interactive tools, my goal remains constant: pairing mathematical rigor with clear, compelling delivery.
I am always keen to collaborate with teams pushing the boundaries of simulation, data science, and scientific computing.
